Definition: from G2596 and G1097; to note against, i.e. find fault with:--blame, condemn.
BiblicalUsage: To find fault is to note the charge and hold it up, and Paul did it to Peter at Antioch because Peter stood blamed for pulling back from the Gentiles. John turns the same word inward: if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and if our heart condemns us not, then we have confidence toward God. The word works both ways, against others and against ourselves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a condemning heart is not the final judge, because God is greater than my heart and knows all things. I hold that honest blame can be a gift when it turns us back, but my confidence rests on Him, not on whether my heart feels clear.
RelatedPeople: Paul; Simon Peter; John the Apostle
